boundary.statement: ingested declarations are adopted only against the frozen audited negative bank; an unsound declaration whose over-accept lies outside that bank passes the certificate, so the shipped kernel must enforce a closed-world trust boundary and prefer UNKNOWN over unsafe inheritance for uncertified declarations

B-DECLARED-FULL.reason: safe+complete support ceiling under the sound declaration

BP-EVASION-CERT-PASS.reason: boundary: a certificate-passing but unsound declaration still yields false accepts; the certificate is closed-world, not a general soundness proof

C-TRAINING-GATE-R-OVERWIDE.reason: comparator: the parent training-consistency gate adopts the over-wide declaration

M-SUPPORT-IDENTITY.reason: induced shipped supports match frozen DESIGN constants

NC-REJECT-ALL.reason: null floor: empty registry accepts nothing and issues no HTTP

PC-CERT-ADMITS-SOUND.reason: certificate admits the sound declared grammar for every family

PC-CERT-REFUSES-OVERWIDE.reason: certificate refuses the training-consistent over-wide declaration for every family

PC-CERT-REFUSES-UNDER.reason: certificate is not a rubber stamp: a too-narrow declaration is refused

PC-DETERMINISM-REPEAT.reason: two independent runs produce identical arm metrics, certificate decisions and identity

PC-DISCRIMINATION.reason: the certificate strictly dominates the training-consistency gate on the audited over-wide class

PC-INGEST-ABSTAIN.reason: on refusal the shipped inferred support is preserved unchanged

PC-UNSAFE-RAW.reason: positive control: unconditional adoption of the over-wide declaration over-accepts

R-UNDER-DETAIL.reason: too-narrow declaration is refused and the shipped support is preserved

T-CERT-GUARD-R-OVERWIDE.reason: PRIMARY: shipped certificate refuses the over-wide declaration; holds the shipped boundary

T-CERT-GUARD-R-SOUND.reason: PRIMARY: shipped certificate adopts the sound declaration; safe+complete

V8_FREEZE_BINDING.reason: hash-bound prereg; running source == FROZEN RUNNER block; freeze artifacts intact
